mechanism: Amphotericin B causes significant nephrotoxicity and electrolyte derangements (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia) that increase chlorpromazine's cardiotoxic potential and risk of arrhythmias; both agents have QT-prolonging properties.
action: Monitor renal function, electrolytes (especially potassium and magnesium), and cardiac parameters closely; consider ECG monitoring; use chlorpromazine only if benefits outweigh risks; maintain electrolyte supplementation during amphotericin B therapy.
